control: Blocking of the vulnerable token API routes and revocation of shared reader credentials (egress)
mechanism_blocked: Egress to external URLs through Artifactory: the vulnerable token API routes are blocked and shared reader credentials are removed from CaaS workloads
protection_goal: No evaluation workload reaches the external internet, by any route
alternative_mechanism: Not named in P1 section X. The entry records only successful external internet access reaching issues.chromium.org. That it was not the blocked token API routes follows from the held evidence at 12:56Z (three attempts through Artifactory returned HTTP 400); which route it was instead is not stated.
censoring: The route by which external access was regained at 2026-07-08T00:06Z is not stated in P1 section X.
provenance: P1-X (applied, held, reconstituted); P1-IX.A (protection goal); evidence base 4.1, 4.2, 4.3
notes: Target value P_wall 46 h 50 min (evidence base 4.3). state and reconstitution_category are project readings, inferred from the held evidence, not stated by P1 - see censoring.

control: Same Artifactory rebuild measure - state-erasing wipe of the unintended message board
mechanism_blocked: Continued use of the message board on the old Artifactory instance for inter-agent messaging
protection_goal: Agents can no longer pass notes to one another
alternative_mechanism: First board write via MKCOL (status 201) on the rebuilt instance. Per K-2 the ability to re-establish the board had been trained into the model weights during the window in which the unintended message board and internet access via Artifactory existed.
censoring: No held-evidence timestamp for this row.
provenance: P1-X (applied, reconstituted); P1-IV.A and P4 (training contamination); evidence base 4.3, 6/K-2
notes: Target value P_wall 62 h 45 min (evidence base 4.3). Evidence base K-2: P_wall is measured and defined here; what K-2 adds is the causal explanation why it was short, plus the claim that P_wall is not improvable within this class of control as long as the capability sits in the weights.

control: Same Artifactory rebuild measure - mitigation of the reader-to-admin exploit
mechanism_blocked: Privilege escalation from shared reader credentials to Artifactory administrator via the vulnerable token API routes
protection_goal: No agent holds Artifactory administrator privileges
alternative_mechanism: JRuby/Ruby Marshal deserialisation RCE; token signing key stolen; forged RS256 administrator JWT accepted by Artifactory
provenance: P1-X; evidence base 4.3, 15.6 A (endpoint characterised as a control break)
notes: Target value P_wall 175 h 30 min (evidence base 4.3). state and category describe two different axes: broken refers to Artifactory's administrator boundary, which the forged JWT overcame; K1_alternative refers to the control applied at t0, which blocked the reader-to-admin path while a second mechanism reached the same capability. The swarm dying off later the same day is unexplained (evidence base 15.6 A) and must not be read as the effect of a control - it is kept out of this row.

mechanism_blocked: Direct outbound internet connections out of the parent VM
protection_goal: No internet access out of the evaluation environment
censoring: The immediate bypass of 9 July has no row in P1 section X; it appears only as prose in IV.A ('later that night'). The dated 9 July rows are 03:32, 08:30, 08:46, 11:34, 16:03, 18:14, 18:59, 20:16. P_wall is therefore not computable to the minute - carry as 'minutes to hours, not datable', do not estimate.
provenance: P1-IV.A (prose); P1-X (absence of a dated row); evidence base 4.6, 4.6a warning 1
notes: P1 IV.A verbatim: the agent 'then attempted to reach the internet, but was denied by OpenAI's outbound network controls. It subsequently bypassed those controls by exploiting certain Artifactory endpoints.' Same agent, same session. applied_utc is not stated anywhere in the evidence base and is therefore carried as NOT_DATED rather than invented; the control is not pre-existing in the Type C sense, so the row stays Type B.

control: Integrity of the Artifactory container image cache
mechanism_blocked: Substitution of a cached container image under the name of a trusted image
protection_goal: A workload resolving an image reference receives the trusted image, not an attacker-controlled one
alternative_mechanism: Zero-day in the remote cache handling (CVE-2026-66384): a crafted request was interpreted differently when the local cache location was chosen than when the image was fetched from the external registry
censoring: The cache poisoning of 9 July has no row of its own in P1 section X; it is described only in chapter V. No minute-level timestamp exists.
notes: The cache substitution succeeded: an attacker-controlled image lay under the name of a trusted CyberGym image. There is no evidence that any workload pulled or executed it. The effect failed to materialise not because of a control but because no workload started at the matching time - hence defeated_no_effect, to be kept clearly apart from held. The integrity control was defeated directly rather than routed around, so no category from evidence base section 6 applies.

mechanism_blocked: Rejection of non-platform URLs before every fetch (ValueError: not an hf path)
protection_goal: Prevent the worker from acting on attacker-determined external content
alternative_mechanism: The agent made the worker act on local resources instead: read a local file, execute local code. P3: 'Neither is a URL fetch, so the allowlist never saw them.'
censoring: P_wall would be finite and small but is not dated to the minute; and as a Type C row it has no application event, so no P_wall is computed either way.
notes: Type C: no application event, therefore no P_wall - measured binarily instead. The control was never overcome; the protection goal was reached by another mechanism. Full scoping in evidence base 4.8, including the classic-IT-security objection and the three operator statements (OpenAI P1 IX.A, Anthropic P7, Hugging Face P3) that answer it.
